result.title: From Relevant Memories to Sufficient Evidence: Rethinking Memory Utilization in LLM Agents
result.summary: Long-term memory enables LLM agents to reuse past experiences, yet retrieving relevant memories does not necessarily provide sufficient evidence for answering a query. Essential information may remain fragmented across memory records, obscured by abstraction, or disconnected from the relations required for reasoning. We identify this relevance-sufficiency gap and propose QEMem, a framework that reformulates memory utilization as the construction of query-specific evidence sets, shifting the focus from individual retrieval relevance to collective evidential support. QEMem integrates three complementary mechanisms: query-guided discovery retrieves evidence across multiple memory granularities; source-grounded reification organizes it into structured ViewCards with explicit evidential roles and source references; and sufficiency-guided refinement selectively recovers missing information. Operating on existing memory stores without modifying memory formation, QEMem achieves 91.43% LLM-judge accuracy on LoCoMo with Claude Opus 4.5, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline, MemR$^3$, by 7.6 percentage points and NEMORI by 10.7 points under a shared memory store. Further analyses demonstrate improved evidence coverage and strong performance on questions requiring cross-session evidence integration.

AI.brief_summary: 论文指出「检索到相关记忆」不等于「证据充分」，提出 QEMem 框架，把记忆利用重构为构建查询相关的证据集合，用查询引导的多粒度发现、带证据角色与来源的结构化 ViewCards、以及充分性引导的补充精化三个机制实现，并在 LoCoMo 上评估。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「充分性引导精化」与证据覆盖分析，可能为 LVR 中视觉证据筛选和「是否停止获取证据」的决策提供线索；但方法作用于文本记忆库、不涉及 latent 状态，迁移可行性需核查。
